title: Puharich first announces his Geller work at Zellerbach Auditorium
summary: Jeffrey Mishlove tells of Puharich first announces his Geller work at Zellerbach Auditorium, about 1972 at Berkeley, California, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: and at Berkeley I sponsored a conference at in Zelerbach auditorium. 1,800 people showed up uh and Puharic was one of the speakers and it was at that conference that he made the very first public announcement about his work with Uri Geller

plain: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena with a doctorate, says that around 1972 he organised a conference at Zellerbach Auditorium in Berkeley, California, and about 1,800 people came. He says one speaker was Andrija Puharich, a doctor who studied people claiming psychic powers, and that this was where Puharich first spoke in public about his work with Uri Geller, a performer who said he could bend metal with his mind. Mishlove tells it as the moment a much-discussed line of psychic research first went public.
